data.title: Spymarks, Not Watermarks
data.author: possibilistic
data.article_summary: 文章提出“spymark（间谍标记）”概念，指未经用户知情同意，隐蔽嵌入图像、音频、文字和视频中的可追踪信号。Google SynthID等技术可编码数据库标识，并与个人信息关联，且能抵抗压缩和再编码。作者认为，“水印”一词掩盖了此类技术的隐私风险，应区分用于认证或版权保护的普通水印与具有监控性质的间谍标记。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“spymarks”（隐形水印/隐写术）的技术原理、应用价值、隐私风险及其可行性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **隐私与监控风险**：Retro_Dev、encrypted_void等认为，社交平台可在图片、视频重新压缩时植入追踪信息，记录内容传播路径、观看者和时间；xp84担心广告商借此实现全流程归因，甚至由设备驱动持续扫描并回传。它可能被用于迫害举报人、识别泄密者，宁可作品被盗也不愿被追踪。  
• **现实中的正当用途**：CM30、swiftcoder、Ennea指出，影视公司、企业内部网页和游戏截图早已使用个性化水印追查泄密者；pavo-etc认为，防伪钞等场景的隐形水印可能是正面应用，SynthID若不降低文本质量也有价值。  
• **技术防护与替代方案**：Retro_Dev建议确保内容与可信生产流程逐字节一致，并认为时间戳加密签名比隐形追踪更安全；itake则以苹果拒绝其移除C2PA元数据的经历，质疑元数据未来能否自由删除。  
• **可靠性与安全性质疑**：gorgoiler指出无法证明水印不存在，验证工具可能同时帮助攻击者确认水印已被清除；若依赖隐藏算法，可能沦为“安全隐 obscurity”。Morromist质疑文本水印的稳定性，词语替换既需足够比特又可能破坏文风。rbtms批评示例过于简陋，难以体现真实应用。  
• **概念与命名争议**：pavo-etc认为“spymark”带有过度负面色彩，“隐形水印”更中性；voidUpdate则追问：若文本由他人创作，如何在不改动内容的情况下植入水印。

补充讨论：评论还提到反水印、社交媒体再压缩、AI本地化与集中化等延伸问题；核心争议是版权保护与防伪价值，是否值得以牺牲匿名性和传播隐私为代价。

49794615.article_content:
There’s a sneaky new evolution of the “watermark”, let’s call it — the spymark.
Spymark
“Spymark”
A
watermark
is a visible mark embedded in a physical or digital medium to verify authenticity or assert ownership.
A
spymark
is a hidden signal that makes your work traceable without your knowledge or consent.
Spymarking is sneaking onto the internet
Google SynthID
is a spymark that embeds secret hidden signals “imperceptible to humans” (Google’s own words) into images, audio, text, and video. This signal can encode database identifiers that map to your identity. Your user records, full name, IP addresses, date of birth, physical addresses, political party affiliation, and more.
Google’s
SynthID-Image paper
reports that its SynthID-O variant can encode a 136-bit payload in a 512x512-pixel image. That is enough room for a 64-bit database identifier, with 72 bits left for error correction.
SynthID was not the first spymark system designed, and it’s hardly the only one under active development.
OpenAI
and many other tech companies are developing these systems at scale. These companies claim spymarking can help identify AI-generated content, yet they’ve gone beyond simple watermarking and built in robust tracking mechanisms. Social media, content production tools, and smartphones may soon find themselves filled with spymarking algorithms that sneak these signals into everything you publish.
For example, images can be invisibly altered in their frequency domain to carry tracking information such as database IDs linked to users:
A smaller version of Mochi’s photo contains a real toy watermark: ID 173, encoded through subtle pixel changes. Compare the original and marked image, animate the amplified differences, and decode the ID from the PNG. The associated author and timestamp are fictional.
Why give it a new name?
“Watermark” has become a catchall for historical marks of authenticity, banknote security features, copyright overlays, and hidden tracking signals in our media. That last usage obscures the privacy risk that some forms of modern “watermarks” have become.
Most people tire of the discourse on privacy. It’s complex, repetitive, and seems irrelevant to the typical day-to-day routine of the average citizen. We can’t keep explaining the technicalities behind statistical tracking tools each and every time we need to communicate these concepts to people and expect them to pay attention.
“To speak the name is to control the thing.” — Ursula K. Le Guin,
The Rule of Names
With a simple change of terminology we can put the privacy concern up front, cementing this issue in the conversation forever:
Spy-
— clandestine surveillance, involuntary disclosure
-mark
— embedded signal
Now we get to disambiguate friendly watermarks from concerning new technology while leveraging the familiar etymology. It collapses a technical communication salient and gains us a lot of ground with just one new word. It’s clear, coherent, and straight to the point.
No more wasting energy establishing the basic facts. The privacy concern is built into the word.
“Spymark” is a privacy
Rumpelstiltskin
.
More spymark examples
Here are a few more forms of spymarks so you can better familiarize yourself.
Audio spymarks operate using principles similar to image spymarks, and they are typically inaudible. Some methods make minute changes to the audio waveform in the time domain; others modify features in the frequency domain, and some combine both approaches. These methods can encode data, including identifiers linked to personal information:
Audio watermark spectrograms
Compare spectrograms of the same LJ Speech excerpt unwatermarked and with Timbre, AudioSeal, WavMark, FSVC, Patchwork, or Norm-Space. The authors’ original plots are linked below.
Spectrograms from Wen et al. (2025),
SoK: How Robust is Audio Watermarking in Generative AI models?
·
Original samples
. Plots retain the authors’ original scales.
These schemes are engineered to be robust. They can often survive compression or re-encoding.
These tools are already proliferating, and in fact they predated generative AI and the push to watermark generative media. The open source spymarking tool
audiowmark
originated in 2018 and can hide 128-bit payloads in audio and protect them with a secret AES key, preventing users without the key from decoding them.
You can even encode personal information invisibly into text!
SynthID steers word choices
to create a detectable statistical pattern that can encode a tracking payload:
An illustrative encoding: eight word choices represent eight bits. The binary value 10101101 gives database ID 173, which can point to a record containing an author and timestamp. These are fictional examples, not a SynthID decoder.
Watermarks are benign, spymarks are not
Watermarks remain easy for the user to spot and are typically not nefarious.
Sometimes watermarks deter counterfeiting:
Sometimes watermarks claim ownership:
Dorothea Lange,
Migrant Mother
(1936) —

data.title: Transformers Explained Visually
data.author: aray07
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕交互式可视化如何解释 Transformer/LLM 的注意力机制、信息流与生成过程，并讨论其技术准确性、适用范围和可用性。

不同观点：
• 机制理解：andblac认为注意力矩阵乘以Value，等同于动态构造并执行一个Dense层；raluk则指出实际按当前token计算时，更适合用“注意力向量”而非完整矩阵理解。mhl47认为多层交替的Attention与MLP会持续混合、查询其他token的信息，因此并非真正把上下文压缩成一个不可解释的向量。  
• 可视化教学：多数评论称赞其直观、易懂；也有人推荐The Illustrated Transformer、bbycroft.net/llm及Token Town作为补充。est则更关心“为什么其他架构没有成功”，认为仅讲工作机制还不够。  
• 技术呈现改进：maciejzj认为Q/K/V权重是注意力的核心，应更早、更突出地展示，并归入各个Attention Head。bilsbie直接提出疑问：独立的Key、Query、Value矩阵究竟分别做什么。  
• 准确性与表述争议：robrenaud认为把temperature与“安全”联系起来不恰当，低温更像缺乏惊喜、机械重复；并建议删除已非现代主流流程中的dropout解释。E-Reverance担心以GPT-2为例会误导初学者，尤其是绝对位置编码已不代表现代模型。  
• 使用体验：hollowturtle批评移动端不兼容，jwpapi称页面甚至导致Chromebook崩溃；另有评论仅表达惊喜或幽默反应。

补充讨论：核心争议在于“面向初学者的简化”与“现代模型的技术准确性”如何平衡；评论也反映出单一可视化难以同时讲清词嵌入、注意力及架构演化。

data.title: Divide by depth for instant 3D
data.author: gabrieloc
data.article_summary: 文章介绍3D图形中的相机原理：最基本的透视投影是将三维坐标的x、y分别除以深度z，使物体越远投影越接近消失点并缩小。通过这一公式可在着色器中绘制球体、线段和立方体等简单几何体。但实际应用还需处理相机位置、朝向、视场角及裁剪面，因此通常使用透视投影矩阵统一实现，并支持视锥体裁剪和性能优化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕3D坐标投影、透视除法、齐次坐标及其教学方式，评论者分享理解、实践经验和扩展应用。

不同观点：
• 技术解释派：指出额外的“1”使3D坐标嵌入四维齐次坐标，从而把本非线性的平移转化为4×4矩阵可处理的线性变换；也有人强调视锥体到NDC及透视除法应从几何直观推导，而非死记矩阵。
• 直觉与自学派：多位评论者回忆在没有线性代数或互联网时，仅凭光影、实验和经验，用QBasic、ZX Spectrum等实现旋转立方体或线框渲染，体现投影公式的直观性。
• 实践展示派：分享HTML5 Canvas、JavaScript等短小3D引擎、互动演示和教学资料，认为滑块和可视化示例能有效降低复杂概念的理解门槛。
• 视觉表现派：认为2D屏幕制造深度不只依赖透视缩小，还包括遮挡、雾化等深度线索；甚至仅靠雾效或遮挡也能形成可信的3D艺术效果。
• 延伸应用派：有人将相关数学用于深度图重建3D场景，也有人希望仅用x′、y′完成完整投影。

补充讨论：评论整体以赞赏和怀旧为主，也提到早期游戏开发者公开传播知识、如今仍有人从原理重新探索；个别项目存在深度排序或数学误差问题。

There are a few ways to construct a perspective projection matrix, depending on your use case. Computer vision and graphics for example, have slightly different conventions for layout, which is why it’s hard to point to a

49769561.article_summary: 文章介绍3D图形中的相机原理：最基本的透视投影是将三维坐标的x、y分别除以深度z，使物体越远投影越接近消失点并缩小。通过这一公式可在着色器中绘制球体、线段和立方体等简单几何体。但实际应用还需处理相机位置、朝向、视场角及裁剪面，因此通常使用透视投影矩阵统一实现，并支持视锥体裁剪和性能优化。
49769561.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕3D坐标投影、透视除法、齐次坐标及其教学方式，评论者分享理解、实践经验和扩展应用。

不同观点：
• 技术解释派：指出额外的“1”使3D坐标嵌入四维齐次坐标，从而把本非线性的平移转化为4×4矩阵可处理的线性变换；也有人强调视锥体到NDC及透视除法应从几何直观推导，而非死记矩阵。
• 直觉与自学派：多位评论者回忆在没有线性代数或互联网时，仅凭光影、实验和经验，用QBasic、ZX Spectrum等实现旋转立方体或线框渲染，体现投影公式的直观性。
• 实践展示派：分享HTML5 Canvas、JavaScript等短小3D引擎、互动演示和教学资料，认为滑块和可视化示例能有效降低复杂概念的理解门槛。
• 视觉表现派：认为2D屏幕制造深度不只依赖透视缩小，还包括遮挡、雾化等深度线索；甚至仅靠雾效或遮挡也能形成可信的3D艺术效果。
• 延伸应用派：有人将相关数学用于深度图重建3D场景，也有人希望仅用x′、y′完成完整投影。

补充讨论：评论整体以赞赏和怀旧为主，也提到早期游戏开发者公开传播知识、如今仍有人从原理重新探索；个别项目存在深度排序或数学误差问题。

data.title: OpenAI is well positioned to fast-follow Jev
data.author: JohnBerryman
data.article_summary: 文章认为，TypeSafe 的 Jev 本质上可能是利用大语言模型下一词概率实现的通用分类器。OpenAI 多年来已在工具调用等场景隐式使用类似机制，因此有望快速复制 Jev，并将其整合进模型和智能体，用于模型选择、提高推理效率、加强安全防护及降低成本。Jev 能否建立护城河，关键取决于其训练数据与训练流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Jev类高效分类模型是否具有长期商业价值，以及OpenAI等前沿实验室是否会复制其技术。

不同观点：
• **技术并不新颖**：orbital-decay认为大型AI公司早已广泛使用各类内部分类器，应用于安全、数据处理、训练和分析；Jev只是让更多人意识到许多生成式任务本质上是分类。  
• **可能被迅速复制**：skybrian、zergrush、nullbio等认为技术壁垒有限，已有开源版本可在普通硬件运行，前沿实验室很快会提供类似API，甚至一天内即可实现。  
• **商业价值存疑**：prometheus1992认为免费替代品众多，Jev效用和商业模式不足；但60secs认为分类器能降低大模型成本、提升吞吐量，因此可能被大厂收购。  
• **与推理模型方向冲突**：andy12认为Jev追求速度、不进行推理，而OpenAI正押注RL推理；若叠加自回归推理，将失去价格和速度优势。  
• **分类概率的可靠性有争议**：amluto指出语言模型的词元概率只是特定训练分布下的条件概率，不等于事实或意图概率；推理过程还会使最终答案概率失真，因此不能直接替代专用分类器。  
• **实际体验支持其价值**：nzoschke在邮件分类中认为Jev比嵌入模型更便捷；gioscarab则主张回归基于固定意图的确定性系统。

补充讨论：评论也批评原文难读、过度聚焦OpenAI和“护城河”，认为真正应讨论接口、基准测试、可切换网关及实际效果。争议核心是：Jev究竟是低门槛的短期热点，还是能显著改善成本、吞吐与开发体验的基础能力。

49802161.article_content:
Will OpenAI Eat Jev's Lunch?
TypeSafe's Jev
introduced a new spin on large language models that has taken the AI world by storm. According to
Vercel
, "Jev was adopted faster than any other model in AI Gateway history." ... But there are clouds forming on the horizon. OpenAI is undoubtedly paying attention – and deciding what to do next.
I wish all the best for TypeSafe, but if they truly live up to their promises, then I'm concerned that OpenAI is well positioned to fast-follow – not only to replicate Jev's flagship product, but also to fold that capability into upcoming models and agents and offer some really useful new behavior that Jev is not positioned to reproduce.
Here is my thesis in brief: OpenAI has for years used their LLMs as implicit classifiers; they just haven't trained them for general classification tasks and they haven't packaged up general classification as a stand-alone product. If OpenAI can replicate the training, then they will be able to replicate Jev in short order. Moreover, OpenAI is positioned to use this new classifier inside of their existing models and agents which can be useful for quick model selection, more efficient thinking, better security guardrails, and generally smarter, faster, and cheaper models.
The key factor deciding all of this is whether or not TypeSafe has a moat to protect themselves. The biggest moat I see is in TypeSafe's training data and training processes.
What's Old Is New Again
Before I make my case, let me state my assumptions and back them up with some relevant history and examples from OpenAI.
My main assumption is that Jev is using something quite close to a conventional large language model. As evidence of this,
Latent Space reports
that many of the early clones are indeed LLM-based.
Here's the idea. Given a
state
and a set of
questions
, Jev's LLM generates a single token or, more accurately, generates the probability distribution over all possible next tokens. The logprobs associated with every possible token at that one step are then massaged into whatever format Jev needs to return. (From here on I'll just say "probabilities" instead of "logprobs" – for our purposes they're interchangeable.)
For a
noul
question, Jev looks at just two tokens,
true
and
false
, ignores everything else, and normalizes their probabilities into a single probability that the answer is
true
. For a
choice
question, Jev can be prompted with a list of possibilities – say
A=happy, B=sad, C=angry, D=afraid
– and it looks at the relative probabilities of those four tokens to build out the full distribution, selecting the highest as the winner. The choice pattern is pretty much what I blogged about way back in 2025 in
Supercharging LLM Classifications with Logprobs
, and even without fine-tuning it was already showing promise. (Sigh... what do they say about ideas and the importance of execution?) I haven't thought hard about the
score
primitive, but I suspect it's a variant of the same pattern.
Part of the premise of this post is that OpenAI might be poised to quickly take advantage of this idea, and this becomes clearer if you understand how. OpenAI has been using large language models implicitly as specialized classifiers since at least the introduction of tool calling.
Back in early 2024 I wrote
Tool Invocation – Demonstrating the Marvel of GPT's Flexibility
, where I coaxed a GPT model into revealing exactly how it decides to call a tool. The following is what a chat session looks like internally. Here there is a user message, then an assistant response without a tool call followed by a user message with a tool call:
I've color-coded the text to indicate token boundaries. If you haven't seen ChatML before, it's the internal markup language that OpenAI introduced for organizing user-agent conversation prompts.
<|im_start|>
and
<|im_end|>
are reserved tokens that delimit the messages, and the first token after
<|im_start|>
identifies the speaker, either
user
or
assistant
.
Right after
<|im_start|>assistant
, the very first token the model predicts is either
\n
or
to=function.
. If it predicts
\n
, it continues on with a normal natural-language response. If it predicts
to=function.
, then that sequence of tokens effectively functions as a classifier deciding whether or not a tool should be invoked at all. The next handful of tokens identify which tool to call –
get_temperature
– another classifier, this time picking from the list of available tools. After that, the model generates argument names, then argument values which can also be vaguely considered as classifiers or estimators. Finally, when the model generates a
<|im_end|>
token, that too is a classifier which reads "true" when the model believes the message is complete.
Some LLMs just don't know when to shut up - a hilarious aside.

data.title: OpenAI GPT–6 Astra breaks Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 文章称，GPT‑6 Astra于2026年独立破解了自2005年未解的德国陆军恩尼格玛电报MVUEH。它通过分析相关电报、发现转录错误和左轮转动规律，并以重复地名“ROSENOW”为线索，自行编写模拟器和Bombe程序，最终找到密钥与明文。该电报与另一封已破解电报内容近乎相同，破解过程及其档案研究能力仍在分析中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM与人类合作破解一条长期未解的恩尼格玛密码信息，以及这一成果对“机器智能、原创性和人类作用”的意义。

不同观点：
• 协作派认为，破解历时两天，Astra提供强大搜索和分析能力，但关键仍在研究者的判断、想象力与方法设计；媒体不应忽略人的主导作用。  
• 技术乐观派认为，LLM若能辅助破解历史密码、数学问题，显示其能力惊人；有人进一步设想其可用于破解“黄道十二宫”密码，甚至创造新的不可破密码。  
• 怀疑派指出，模型可能主要依赖既有资料、模拟器和大量尝试，并不等于具备原创思维；面对全新问题，仍需要想象力和跳出框架的能力。  
• 批评派担忧智能被资本和算力商品化，甚至认为顶尖人类智力正变得可替代；也有人觉得企业把资源投入冷门数学问题既“惊人”又缺乏实际意义。  
• 质疑者怀疑“Astra提到私人收藏”是否涉及未授权数据或黑客行为，但尚无明确证据。

补充讨论：评论补充了密文及其大意：“请说明行军路线……我在罗斯诺……立即无线电回复”；还提到原抄本有误、该信息使用不同日钥、转子在第72字符处转动，导致常规攻击失效。另有人询问“2005”的关联、未破译语言及其他历史密码。争议焦点是成果究竟体现了LLM的原创推理，还是依赖数据、算力与人类指导。

49801324.article_content:
OpenAI GPTâ6 Astra breaking an Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005.
On 15 September 2026, Carter Leffer contacted me to request validation of a break of the German Army Enigma message MVUEH of 10 July 1941. The message, which was sent by a radio station with the tactical callsign 2ny, was received by the radio station of the SS-Totenkopf Quartiermeister, Ib. Ib received the message at 17:30 on 10 July 1941 and logged the message as Nr. 172 in its log of incoming messages for July 1941. Since 2005, the message has resisted all attempts to break it.
On 9 June 2017, Alex Shovkoplyas succeeded in breaking another unbroken message from this day, Nr. 173, SIPVX. However, the Enigma key he recovered for the message differed slightly from the daily Enigma key for 10 July 1941 used for all other messages from this day. The SIPVX key used the same wheel order, 512, as the daily key, but the plug connections (
Stecker
) and ring setting (
Ringstellung
) differed. However, the new key did not allow us to break the MVUEH message.
After Carter Leffer sent the MVUEH break details, it was immediately clear he had found the correct key and plaintext. The MVUEH key turns out to be completely different from the other keys from 10 July 1941; even the wheel order differs: 253 instead of 512 for the other two keys. More surprising is that the plaintext is almost identical to the plaintext for message Nr. 173, SIPVX. The two messages differ in length by twelve letters. MVUEH is 82 letters long, while SIPVX has 94 letters. This difference is due to a mistake when enciphering the word Bitte in MVUEH, which resulted in Btte, and to the senderâs signature, Waschbusch, being repeated in the SIPVX message.
An analysis of the break revealed that the transcription of the MVUEH ciphertext from the original message form contained several errors, and the break revealed that the Enigmaâs left-hand wheel makes a turnover at the 72nd letter. A turnover of the Enigmaâs left-hand wheel, which rarely occurs, is known to complicate a break. These factors may have prevented an earlier break.
However, the most astonishing thing about this break is that the GPTâ6 Astra did it entirely on its own. Carter Leffer only directed GPTâ6 Astra to see if it could break any of the unbroken Enigma messages published on the Crypto Cellar Research web page. After analysing the unbroken messages on the website, it decided that the most promising message was Nr. 172, MVUEH and it also quickly suspected that the plaintext of Nr. 173, SIPVX, might be related to the plaintext of the unbroken MVUEH message. After trying many different approaches, GPTâ6 Astra focused on using the repeated place name ROSENOW ROSENOW as a crib. After developing the necessary Python and C++ software for an Enigma simulator and an Enigma Bombe, GPTâ6 Astra started a thorough break with the ROSENOW crib, which in the end resulted in the correct key and plaintext for the MVUEH message being found.
We are still analysing the GPTâ6 Astra logs to see exactly how it executed the break. And we are discovering amazing details. In July 2026, I made the following announcement on the webpage with the 1941 Message List:
Note: In July 2026, research in the German Bundesarchiv revealed several
collections of radio messages, both enciphered and in cleartext. One of
these message collections was from SS-Totenkopf Divisionâs logistics
command, NachschubfÃ¼hrer. Many of these messages were sent to the Ib
(Quartiermeister) radio station and are identical to those in this list.
Others are new, but most likely related. These new messages are added to
the 1941 Message List in bold, with the indicator NF (NachschubfÃ¼hrer)
after the message number, indicating that these message numbers belong
to the NF numbering. All NF messages are outgoing; hence, the message
numbers are in blue.
It appears that GPTâ6 Astra discovered this note about the collections of radio messages at the German Bundesarchiv, because in one of the logs we find the following:
Original-source access lead.
The completed evidence pass traced the received corpus to a private collection and found concrete Bundesarchiv radio-message volumes, including RS 3â3/20a and RS 3â3/63b. Catalogue records have been inspected; the original received no.172 image remains unlocated, and the available archive viewer has not yet exposed the relevant scans in this environment. No correspondence has been sent.
The file references GPTâ6 Astra mentions, RS 3â3/20a and RS 3â3/63b, are correct, but they are not available on the Crypto Cellar Research website. GPTâ6 Astra mentions a private collection, but it is not clear what this is, whether it has succeeded in accessing the Bundesarchivâs digitised collections or whether it has found these files elsewhere. What is clear, though, is that GPTâ6 Astra is behaving like a very professional cryptanalyst and archive researcher. What it has achieved in two days would take

data.title: Apple has added persistent 'ads' to iOS, and it's driving users crazy
data.author: MC995
data.article_summary: 苹果在iOS“设置”顶部推送iCloud+、Apple Music、Apple TV和AppleCare+等自家服务促销，被用户视为广告。部分提示无法关闭，可能持续数周甚至数月，并伴随通知徽章；即使已订阅相关服务，也有人仍看到推送。用户对此强烈不满，认为苹果借助服务业务增长而侵扰体验，相关问题也可能源于系统漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论集中讨论苹果在系统、应用和服务中增加广告及促销内容，是否损害了其一贯的简洁、克制和用户信任形象。

不同观点：
• 强烈反对者认为，App Store、Apple Maps、设置、iCloud等出现广告、升级提示和红点提醒，像“广告填满的灾难”，与乔布斯“不想要广告”的理念背离；苹果已有巨额利润，继续榨取用户源于增长压力和缺乏创新。
• 部分用户认为这反映了苹果产品整体体验恶化：原生应用臃肿、备份和iCloud免费空间不足、系统强制更新、暗黑模式诱导购买或启用功能，甚至让人考虑转向Android、GrapheneOS、Linux或Home Assistant。
• 有人认为广告泛滥是更广泛的社会和产品问题。广告制造持续噪音，推动产品越来越差；使用翻盖手机等无广告设备能明显感受到这种变化。
• 较温和或支持苹果的一方认为，推荐的只是有价值的配套产品，位置合理且可以关闭，并非侵入式弹窗或恶意推销，用户仍可选择不购买。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“合理的产品推荐”与“未经欢迎的广告/诱导升级”如何界定。评论还指出，相关媒体一边批评广告一边展示苹果广告，进一步凸显讽刺；也有人质疑新系统版本是否加剧问题。

iOS users are seeing ‘ads’ for other Apple products on their iPhones
The banners promote services like iCloud+, Apple Music and AppleCare+
The messages often can’t be dismissed and stick around for weeks
If you were to ask iOS users how they felt about
Apple
’s decision to
insert ads into Apple Maps
, it would quickly become obvious that it was
not a popular move
. So when iPhone fans discovered that Apple has been inserting prompts for its own products into iOS, the reaction was predictably swift and furious.
The ‘ads’ in question appear in the Settings app in iOS. They can be found near the top of the iPhone’s display and promote several products to the user, including paid-for
iCloud+
storage, free trials for services like
Apple Music
and
Apple TV
, and the
AppleCare+
extended warranty.
Infuriatingly for iOS users, the only way to disable these promos is to either let them expire — which in many cases could take weeks or even months, leaving a persistent notification badge on the Settings app in the meantime — or pay for the service being offered. There is not always a “dismiss” button to shoo them away for good, and when there is, some people have reported that
it doesn’t seem to work
.
Latest Videos From
TechRadar
Watch full video here:
Many people have taken to social media to vent their frustrations with Apple’s actions. “I’m feeling like this is nearly on-par with the ens***ification that
Microsoft
introduced with Start menu ads,”
said one aggravated user
. “I wish Apple would just stop that crap,” stated another.
Many other people
have
taken to Reddit
to
express their exasperation
, suggesting that the discontent is widespread.
Some of these ads and offers — such as the one for Apple Music — appear after you’ve bought a new Apple product. With the company launching the
iPhone Duo
and
iPhone 18 Pro
range recently, it’s perhaps unsurprising that we’re seeing a sudden influx of posts flush with irritation and indignation.
You may like

Apple’s expensive, inflexible app subscriptions need a total overhaul — here's why
Windows 11 desktop becomes a huge Harry Potter ad thanks to Bing Wallpaper
Apple’s services push
(Image credit: Future)
On the face of it, Apple’s decision to include promotions like this in its
operating system
might seem like a strange one. After all, Apple has long positioned itself as a premium company where the user experience is paramount. From that viewpoint, repeatedly attempting to prod customers towards even more of the company’s products might seem cheap, even distasteful. And when you’ve just shelled out a record fee for an iPhone after Apple’s
painful price rises
, that can just feel like nickel and diming.
But Apple has been putting increasing emphasis on its services in recent years, of which products like
iCloud
+, Apple Music, Apple TV and AppleCare+ are all a part. With limited room for growth in the smartphone market, the company is turning to areas where it thinks it can make more progress.

And unfortunately for users, that means more ads like this on their devices. While they are far from the most obnoxious ads around, the fact that many cannot be dismissed is clearly rubbing users the wrong way — as is the fact that the promos even exist at all in an Apple product.
There is also the possibility that at least some of these adverts are appearing due to a bug. The iCloud+ one in particular has drawn comments from users who are already subscribed to iCloud+ and thus, one would think, should not need to see any ads like this. Time will tell how that plays out and whether Apple fixes this ‘bug’ or leaves the ads in place. If the latter transpires, it would suggest that they are not appearing erroneously.
With Apple’s services push showing no signs of slowing down and
further ads supposedly planned
for the likes of the firm’s
Visual Intelligence
system, don’t expect Apple to have a change of heart any time soon.

Quantum Physics
arXiv:2609.05472
(quant-ph)
[Submitted on 21 Aug 2026]
Title:
Quantum information spreading via higher-order operator correlators
Authors:
M Süzen
View a PDF of the paper titled Quantum information spreading via higher-order operator correlators, by M S\"uzen
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We provide a perspective into measuring the quantum information spreading by introducing N-operator correlators. Leveraging the idea from N-point correlation function from cosmology, we formulate a generalized Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC), called N-Operator Correlator (NOC). Such formulation can reduce the effect of restricted analysis associated with selecting only two operators for OTOC. NOC can take into account a larger set of measurement probes in measuring the degree of quantum information spreading. We demonstrate these concepts with two analytically tractable toy systems with computing thermal averages of operator time evolutions at a finite temperature: a single qubit in longitudinal field and XYZ two-qubit system. Our perspective serves as a basic introduction to generalized operator correlators in quantum mechanics.

What is Jev?
Jev is TypeSafe AI's model for answering typed questions about text or JSON: choose an option, estimate whether something is true, or score it against a rubric. Use it for bounded decisions such as routing, ranking, or selecting an agent's next action; use a generative LLM when you need new prose, code, or an open-ended plan. Your application still controls permissions, validation, and execution.

data.title: We broke an Over-The-Air update on the ESP32 on purpose
data.author: adunk
data.article_summary: 文章强调OTA更新对联网产品至关重要，但必须具备不可破坏性和自动恢复能力。更新应实现“要么完整应用，要么保持原版本”，即使下载中断、软件/硬件重启或断电也不能变砖，并应自动重试完成升级。作者使用Groundrun在ESP32-C6上模拟三种中断场景，验证系统恢复能力及耗时，建议将此类测试纳入每次系统变更后的开发流程。
data.comments_summary:

49776999.article_content:
Over-The-Air (OTA) updates are one of the most fundamental mechanisms in any connected product. Thanks to OTAs, we can fix problems even after the product has shipped simply by downloading a new firmware over the air. In fact, most connected products perform an OTA update the first thing they do when they are installed: this ensures they always have all the latest fixes as quickly as possible.
OTAs entirely change the entire software in our system, so they are delicate: there are plenty of chances where the mechanism could go wrong. (This is why you sometimes see a message saying "do not switch off until the update is applied".)
But because the OTA mechanism is so important, it has to be completely reliable. There should be no way to break the OTA mechanism, no matter how hard we try. Even if we download only a partial OTA, or if power is cut at the worst possible moment. Nothing should break it. And we should recover as quickly as possible.
OTAs are such an important mechanism that it must be automatically tested on every change to the system. We should have our devices go through the worst possible ways we could wreck havoc to the update mechanism, and see that they still work. The update needs to either fully apply or not apply at all: if the update fails, we should be back at a known-good state.
We need to:
Survive
the interruption. The device should still be alive after an interrupted OTA update, running the original version of the code.
Recover
from the interruption. The device should redo the OTA update, thus ending up on the new version of the code.
So this we need to test: an update either finishes and applies cleanly, or it gets interrupted. The power goes out mid-download, the device reboots on its own, someone hits reset at the wrong moment. When that happens, the device has to recover on its own and finish the job anyway.
In this post we use the Groundrun system to try to crush OTAs on an ESP32-C6 system and to see that we are able to successfully recover every time. We kill the OTA in three different ways: (1) we do a software reset in the middle of the update, (2) we do a hardware reset in the middle of the update, and (3) we pull the power plug on the entire system in the middle of the update. We then ensure that the system is able to recover, restart the update, and complete it. We measure the time it is able to do so.
This is something that any connected product should do as part of its development workflow to ensure that the system is as stable as possible, after every change to the system.
How Over the air updates work
An over-the-air update pushes new firmware to a device over its own network connection, then installes the new firmware to itself. The new image comes from a cloud backend, which knows both which version each device is running and which version the device shold be updated to. Whether the device fetches it right away depends on the product: some updates apply quietly in the background, and others show up in the app first, so the person using the product decides when to accept one. Either way, the device downloads the new image, applies it, and reboots into it.
New image
ready in the cloud
Sent in the
background
Shown in the
app first
Device
downloads it
Applies and
reboots into it
A new image starts in the cloud, reaches the device either quietly or through the app, and the device applies it.
The tricky part is if the OTA process gets interrupted. In the worst case, a firmware image applied halfway through a write can leave a device unable to boot at all, which is the absolutely worst state that a connected product can end up in. This is typically known as a
bricked
device: a device that is about as useful as a brick. Completely dead to the world.
Any OTA mechanism must be fully able to avoid bricking the device. The common defense is to never touch the firmware a device is currently running until the new image has confirmed itself. The new image goes into its own separate storage first, gets verified before anything switches over, and the device falls back to what it was running if the new image never completes. Today, every chip vendor provides an OTA mechanism that has this level of production. In our case, the Espressif's ESP-IDF, which the ESP32 in this experiment runs, is one of them. With the default mechanism, an interrupted update cannot leave a device unable to boot.
Since the OTA mechanim protects us against bricking the device, the worst state we can end up in is a device stuck on the old version, with nothing making sure a fresh attempt ever happens. Our system must therefore be able to detect this and recover. We should automatically start a new attempt with the end goal that our device ends up on the target version.

ESP32
is
Espressif

data.title: MUNI Heritage Weekend in San Francisco
data.author: plun9
data.article_summary: 作者参加2026年旧金山Muni传统周末活动，用线阵相机拍摄多辆历史有轨电车，包括Muni 1号、162号、578号、墨尔本、米兰及黑池船式电车等，并介绍其年代、来源和特色。作者还展示了其他PCC电车、Waymo车辆和警车照片，说明部分拍摄受车辆遮挡、相机震动及失焦影响。所有电车照片以CC BY-SA 4.0授权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用线阵扫描相机拍摄旧金山Muni复古有轨电车，作品的视觉效果、拍摄技术及公共资源使用争议。

不同观点：
• 多数评论称赞照片“美丽”“令人惊叹”，认为画面像建筑图纸；特别提到1912年的车辆和1896年的“Dinky”，并肯定作者为拍摄轨迹观察、投入数小时的过程。  
• 技术讨论者推测车辆是垂直于镜头方向经过，因此主要呈现侧面，并询问车辆斜向经过时的成像效果，以及所用镜头是否需要覆盖135画幅。  
• 有人提醒在公共场所架设三脚架、形成绊倒风险时，应考虑购买公共责任保险。  
• 质疑者指出，Muni正面临预算短缺、削减公交线路和班次，却持续为仅供自身运营的复古车辆定制零件、维持专业修复团队；因此认为这些项目脱离财政背景看很酷，但可能不负责任。  
• 另一条评论强调Muni几乎每个周末都运营复古线路或将F线作为博物馆运营，实际上支持了对其资源投入必要性的质疑。

补充讨论：争议焦点不在照片质量，而在公共交通经费紧张时，保存和运营历史车辆是否值得、是否应优先于日常公交服务。

data.title: Show HN: Drop – a rootless Linux sandbox with gVisor support
data.author: mixedbit
data.article_summary: Drop 是一款无需 root 的 Linux 沙箱工具，用于隔离编码代理和第三方程序。它创建可丢弃环境，隐藏真实主目录，限制文件、目录及本地网络访问，防止误删、提示注入和恶意软件造成损害。Drop 基于现有发行版运行，无需容器配置，并支持 TOML 配置及 gVisor 内核，提供额外安全隔离。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一种面向 AI Agent/程序运行的 Linux 沙箱工具，讨论其安全模型、与现有工具的差异、跨平台可能性及实际使用价值。

不同观点：
• saghm 认为该工具接近其理想需求：禁止写入指定目录外的文件，同时保留大范围读取权限，避免手动复制依赖；相比 bubblewrap 配置方案，它更完整、更专注 Linux。其特别关注任意 GUI 应用支持，计划实际测试，并批评大公司仍主要依赖不透明规则或繁琐的命令白名单。
• refibrillator 认为类似项目正在增多，说明需求真实、方向有价值。但指出文档对安全差异说明不足：工具似乎仍基于 nsjail、runc 等采用的相同底层机制，因此质疑为何不直接构建在这些成熟原语之上。
• zoobab 提出可比较 Proot：它不使用进程命名空间，且能在 Android/Termux（如 proot-distro）运行，暗示跨平台和兼容性也是选择方案时的重要因素。
• JoshTriplett 询问核心优势是否在于增加程序与内核系统调用之间的隔离层，聚焦其相对 bubblewrap 的关键安全改进。
• yu3zhou4 对项目表示祝贺，认为此类能力有助于 AI 工具获得安全性方面的普及，并推荐更详细的沙箱文档。

补充讨论：争议焦点是该工具是否提供了超越现有 namespace、系统调用过滤等机制的实质安全增益，以及其易用性（读取权限、GUI 支持）与安全强化之间如何平衡。

49801329.article_content:
Linux sandboxing that doesn’t get in your way
Isolate programs and coding agents without leaving your familiar work environment
Install Drop
Use cases
Isolate coding agents
Run agents with
--dangerously-skip-permissions
and let Drop enforce
permissions at the OS level. A hallucinated
rm -rf ~
doesn’t touch
your actual home dir. A prompt injection targeting
~/.ssh
finds
nothing. A connection to services running on localhost is rejected.
Isolate third-party programs
Install programs from PyPI, npm or any other source without giving
them full access to your user account. If an installed program is
malicious or compromised in a supply chain attack, the damage is
contained within the sandbox.
How it works
Disposable, isolated environments
Inspired by Python’s virtualenv, Drop lets you create and enter easily
disposable environments. Each environment has its own home
directory while the original home is hidden.
Your existing distribution
Unlike Docker/Podman, Drop uses your existing distribution, so there
is no container setup work: every program you’ve already installed is
available in the sandbox.
Flexible config language
High-level TOML config lets you specify which files, dirs and local
network services should be exposed to the sandbox. By default, all Drop
environments share a base config, so you can configure Drop once and
then create new environments without any configuration work.
Rootless
Drop doesn’t require root to run. It runs within a Linux user
namespace, with its own process, mount, network, IPC and cgroup
namespaces. Drop drops all the user namespace capabilities before
executing a sandboxed program, so the program cannot do privileged
operations within the user namespace, like bind mounts.
gVisor integration
As an option, Drop supports running programs on the gVisor user-space
kernel. This is an additional isolation layer that prevents programs
from accessing the host kernel directly, significantly reducing
the potential to exploit kernel vulnerabilities.

• saghm 认为该工具接近其理想需求：禁止写入指定目录外的文件，同时保留大范围读取权限，避免手动复制依赖；相比 bubblewrap 配置方案，它更完整、更专注 Linux。其特别关注任意 GUI 应用支持，计划实际测试，并批评大公司仍主要依赖不透明规则或繁琐的命令白名单。
• refibrillator 认为类似项目正在增多，说明需求真实、方向有价值。但指出文档对安全差异说明不足：工具似乎仍基于 nsjail、runc 等采用的相同底层机制，因此质疑为何不直接构建在这些成熟原语之上。
• zoobab 提出可比较 Proot：它不使用进程命名空间，且能在 Android/Termux（如 proot-distro）运行，暗示跨平台和兼容性也是选择方案时的重要因素。
• JoshTriplett 询问核心优势是否在于增加程序与内核系统调用之间的隔离层，聚焦其相对 bubblewrap 的关键安全改进。
• yu3zhou4 对项目表示祝贺，认为此类能力有助于 AI 工具获得安全性方面的普及，并推荐更详细的沙箱文档。

补充讨论：争议焦点是该工具是否提供了超越现有 namespace、系统调用过滤等机制的实质安全增益，以及其易用性（读取权限、GUI 支持）与安全强化之间如何平衡。

data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary: Meta推出的AI助手Muse可代办事务、操作账户并访问 macOS 多项敏感权限。安全专家发现其零日漏洞：本地应用或终端命令可篡改设置，将语音转写地址改为攻击者服务器，从而窃取账户令牌并控制助手，执行写入恶意文件、拍照等操作。该设计暴露出Meta在安全和隐私测试上的不足，亚马逊也已禁止Muse购物。

• 该评论隐含强调权限最小化原则：AI 应只获得完成任务所必需的权限，而不应拥有过大的系统权限。

Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has gone to
great lengths
to hype the security of its new AI assistant, Muse, claiming it is “built from the ground up for privacy and security.” A zero-day vulnerability that gives locally run apps and terminal commands complete control of the agent raises serious doubts. Further raising questions, Amazon on Sunday began blocking Muse from its site.
Meta
introduced
Muse a few weeks ago. The assistant “books appointments, fills out forms and handles customer service,” “proactively takes tasks off your plate,” and can “make purchases, generate images, create documents, and connect with your favorite apps and services.” The macOS app (curiously, there’s no Windows version) also works with a user’s WhatsApp, email, calendar, and social media accounts. When a task requires a tool that doesn’t exist, Muse creates one on the fly.
Meta doth hype Muse security too much
Of course, for Muse to do any of these things, users must first give it access to their accounts. This includes authenticating the assistant to each service and, because the app runs on macOS, giving it permissions to a broad range of operating system-restricted device resources, like writing files to disk, accessing the mic and camera, and monitoring location and calendars. Apple has spent years developing these defenses to prevent installed apps or commands entered into the terminal from accessing these resources, clearly because the company considers them a security threat. Muse completely undoes these default measures.
The
zero-day
allows any app or terminal command to gain access to the token that authenticates users to their Muse account. Meta developers designed the assistant so that any locally installed app or executed code, regardless of the macOS permissions it has, can change a long list of undocumented settings. Most of them are fairly innocuous, such as controlling dark mode. One setting, however, is anything but innocuous. It allows processes to change the endpoint where transcription occurs. Normally, it’s a server address operated by Meta. Attackers can exploit this flaw by changing the location to their own endpoint. Once that happens, the attackers have the token that gives complete control over the Muse account.
“We can manipulate the agent and leverage its privileges to do whatever we want,” Patrick Wardle, the macOS security expert who discovered the zero-day, told Ars. “So instead of us having to write a very comprehensive Mac malware stealer, we can just leverage the AI assistant itself.” Wardle said he has developed several proof-of-concept attacks that do things like writing malicious files to disk and snapping pictures, in many cases with no indication to even an alert user.
Meta representatives didn’t answer emailed questions.
Meta has published
two
posts
in as many weeks documenting the design decisions that went into ensuring an assistant with such extraordinary access to user data and resources is secure and private. The posts come amid revelations that internal testing of models from
Anthropic
and
Google
has resulted in security breaches of external, third-party networks that the engineers involved never intended to target. In traditional human-only hacking, these actions could likely result in the filing of criminal charges. The Meta posts are likely mindful of the resulting blowback and the calls to slow down AI development in response.
Wardle said that Meta developers made several design decisions that made his exploit possible. One is the choice for Muse dictation to occur in the cloud, where Meta can log it. macOS has long provided a simple means for apps to handle dictation and transcription in processes that stay securely on the device. Had the developers chosen this safer alternative, the attack wouldn’t have been possible.
Another flawed decision is for any app to control all of the undocumented settings. It’s likely Meta intended for apps working with Muse to control UI settings, and for understandable reasons. The ability for any app or command to control an endpoint where sensitive user speech is processed is an entirely different matter. Together, the design decisions raise questions about just how much effort developers put into designing and testing the security and privacy of the new assistant.
“To me, the bar is infinitely higher in terms of the security of these apps. They don’t have to be perfect, but when you take a look at Muse, it’s like they didn’t, in my opinion, think about security, which is really worrisome,” Wardle said. “At the very least, they should be thinking about security from the very start, and they are just not.”
Roughly 12 hours before Wardle disclosed the zero-day, Amazon started blocking people from using Muse to shop on the site. Users who tried received a message saying Muse was an “unauthorized AI age

data.title: AMD's random number generator can't generate a 0?
data.author: BruceEel
data.article_summary: 文章讨论AMD处理器上`RDRAND`和`RDSEED`生成随机数的问题：以16位寄存器读取时似乎永远无法得到真正的0，而英特尔处理器正常。测试显示，改用32位或64位寄存器生成，再取低16位即可出现0。参与者还讨论了硬件随机数的安全性及是否应混合其他熵源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD Zen 2 处理器的 RDRAND16 可能永不返回 0，以及该硬件随机数缺陷的影响、成因与验证。

不同观点：
• [jstanley]指出 Zen 2 曾出现 RDRAND 恒返回全 1 的漏洞，怀疑此次是否变成“永不返回全 0”；实测 Ryzen 5 3600 的 RDRAND32 正常，但 RDRAND16 确实无法生成 0。  
• [CodesInChaos]认为实际影响可能有限，因为硬件随机数通常只用于播种 CSPRNG，而非直接作为安全随机数。  
• [strenholme]主张在安全场景使用 XOF，将多次 RDRAND、系统时间、网络间隔等熵源混合，以避免固定缺陷造成明显偏差。  
• [matja]在 Zen 3 上观察到 16 位随机数可生成 0，暗示问题可能仅限部分 Zen 2，或已在后续版本修复。  
• [20k]关注硬件验证为何未发现该问题；[hnacobsxph]补充称，直方图能发现偏差，而常规统计测试可能漏检。

补充讨论：争议焦点包括缺陷是否扩展到 32/64 位、零值是否被映射为其他固定值、RDRAND 是否由多次内部读取组成，以及该偏差对实际密码学安全性的影响。AMD 官方公告链接也被提供；部分评论带有玩笑或对“随机生成 0”的误解。

Recently, while doing some assembly code to render data intro charts, and using 'rdrand' and 'rdseed' to provide that data to the displayed, I've figured out by accident what appears to be a bug (problem) only with AMD processors (maybe Zen2 only problem): they can't generate a number 0 at a given size! Running the same programs on  an Intel processor, and the 0's are there with no problem.
You can help me figure out this by using my
application
to seek for any 0 number generated, and maybe post your results at this forum thread...
I also must mention that this application is a very deep showcase on how to control and render data to the console screen at arbitrary positions, which I remember someone here was trying to achieve the same under Linux cli, and he asked for help on this subject before.
Attached, I've provided that exact chart test application that showcases the AMD's RNG 0 problem: you'll probably, on an AMD host, never see the first bar change colors from green (which uses a TSC method I've created to generate random numbers), and also never see the base chart scale up from 0. On Intel processor, no problem, and the chart scale its base (minimum) beyond 0. The first bar renders how many zeroes are being generated by rdrand (red), rdseed (blue) and TSC-custom technique (green), as well as other bars render the other 65535 numbers from the 16-bit space.
Note: it requires
fastcall_v1 macro kit
if anyone wants to compile and test it as is.
Cheers!

data.title: A font that reads what you wrote
data.author: RohanAdwankar
data.article_summary: semfont 是一个自动优化排版的轻量库，通过为每个词计算情感倾向、显著性、意外度和确定性，将其映射为颜色、字重、高亮和斜体。算法结合词典、上下文、重复率及句法规则，并新增整分句分析，处理否定、因果、比较和讽刺等复杂语义，同时记录每次调整原因，便于调试与解释。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款依据语义分析为文本着色/强调的工具，讨论其新颖性、可用性、阅读体验及技术实现。

不同观点：
• 赞赏其概念：有人认为这是“自然语言的语法高亮”，能揭示文本理解、显著性和节奏；即使实现尚不成熟，想法本身也很有价值。  
• 质疑阅读体验：高亮造成强迫感、语义噪声和不协调，像拙劣的AI写作或小学语法课；有人认为读者应自行判断重点，担心普及后损害自主阅读。  
• 认为用途有限但有潜力：适合个人笔记、录音转写、PDF/LaTeX中的语法式标注，并应允许用户调整；不适合公开写作，以免制造非预期含义。  
• 担忧被滥用：若用于邮件或Slack，管理者可能据颜色评判员工“红字太多、绿字太少”。也有人以隐私为例，担心未来字体向厂商反馈阅读内容。  
• 技术与定位争议：Firefox无法运行、Chrome兼容性问题；有人批评它并非真正的“字体”而是JS库，标题夸大，另有人原以为计算逻辑内置于字体中。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“概念创新”与“实际帮助/阅读干扰”的权衡，以及语义标注应由个人控制还是可能成为外部评价工具。

49774161.article_content:
semfont
is a small library that sets typography automatically.
As you can see below it automatically highlights, colors, bolds, and italicizes text which aims to make it easier to read.
theme
editorial
loud
monochrome
technical
How it works
Every word gets four scores. Each one starts as a dictionary lookup and is then adjusted by a couple of rules over the words around it.
Valence
is how good or bad the word is, from -1 to 1. A negator up to three words back flips the sign and damps it, because
not great
is a mild complaint rather than the mirror image of praise. An intensifier up to two words back scales it instead.
let v = VALENCE[word] ?? 0;          // great -> 0.75
if (negatorWithin(3)) v = -v * 0.74; // not great -> -0.55
v *= gain;                           // really great -> 0.98
Salience
is how much the word is worth looking at, 0 to 1. A frequency list gives each word a rarity, 0 for one of the hundred most common English words and 1 for one it has never seen. Rarity alone is not enough, so the score also rises with how often the word repeats in this particular text: an uncommon word you keep saying is what the text is about.
const seen = Math.min(1, (repeats - 1) / 2);
const repetition = 0.45 + 0.55 * seen;
let s = SALIENCE[word] ?? 0;
s = Math.max(s, 0.55 * rarity * repetition);
// rarity('the') 0.00, rarity('kubelet') 0.93
// kubelet said once   -> 0.23
// kubelet said 3 times -> 0.51
Surprise
is where the sentence turns, 0 to 1. Some words announce it on their own, like
suddenly
or
ironically
. Otherwise it comes from position: everything for six words after a contrast word gets it, decaying with distance, and so does any word much rarer than the rest of the passage.
let s = SURPRISE[word] ?? 0;         // suddenly -> 0.85
if (afterContrast) {
s = Math.max(s, 0.45 * 0.82 ** (distance - 1));
}
s += 0.3 * Math.max(0, rarity - passageMeanRarity - 0.25);
// 'The tests failed'            -> failed 0.16
// 'It compiled, but the tests failed' -> failed 0.44
Certainty
is how sure the writer sounds, -1 hedged to 1 asserted. Words like
probably
and
definitely
are in a table. But if you write
The build probably failed
, you are not unsure about the word
probably
, you are unsure about whether it failed. So the hedge keeps its own score and every other word in the sentence gets 55% of it, and the whole line leans a little instead of one word in the middle of it.
c = CERTAINTY[word] ?? sentenceCertainty * 0.55;
// 'The build probably failed.'
// probably -0.40, every other word -0.22
Then a theme maps each score to one typographic axis: valence to colour, salience to weight, surprise to a highlight, certainty to slant. Each axis has a threshold, so most words come out untouched.
Improving the algorithm
Those rules only look a few words either side, and that window has a blind spot. Write
I would not go so far as to call the new editor great
and
great
stays green, because the
not
that cancels it sits nine words back. Write
We fixed the crash
and you get one green word and one red one, because nothing connects
fixed
to the thing it fixed.
So a second pass now runs after the window rules and reads each clause as a whole. A negator reaches to the end of its clause and fades with distance, which turns
great
red. A verb like
fixed
,
recovered
or
avoided
marks whatever follows it as the thing that got better, which turns
crash
green. The same pass reads
less broken
and
fewer complaints
as improvements,
too simple
as a complaint, and a lone
Great,
in front of bad news as sarcasm.
Every change it makes is recorded on the word, so you can ask why a word came out the colour it did:
analyze('We fixed the crash.').tokens[6];
// { text: 'crash', valence: 0.44,
//   notes: ['resolved by "fixed"'] }
It costs about as much as the first pass and stays inside the budget, so there is no switch to flip. These are the ten sentences that led to it, including those two. Left is the first version, right is now.
before
now
Great, another outage. Just what I needed today.
Great, another outage. Just what I needed today.
We fixed the crash and closed the security hole before anyone noticed.
We fixed the crash and closed the security hole before anyone noticed.
The cluster recovered from the crash in under a minute.
The cluster recovered from the crash in under a minute.
We avoided a catastrophic outage by catching the bug in staging.
We avoided a catastrophic outage by catching the bug in staging.

49774161.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款依据语义分析为文本着色/强调的工具，讨论其新颖性、可用性、阅读体验及技术实现。

不同观点：
• 赞赏其概念：有人认为这是“自然语言的语法高亮”，能揭示文本理解、显著性和节奏；即使实现尚不成熟，想法本身也很有价值。  
• 质疑阅读体验：高亮造成强迫感、语义噪声和不协调，像拙劣的AI写作或小学语法课；有人认为读者应自行判断重点，担心普及后损害自主阅读。  
• 认为用途有限但有潜力：适合个人笔记、录音转写、PDF/LaTeX中的语法式标注，并应允许用户调整；不适合公开写作，以免制造非预期含义。  
• 担忧被滥用：若用于邮件或Slack，管理者可能据颜色评判员工“红字太多、绿字太少”。也有人以隐私为例，担心未来字体向厂商反馈阅读内容。  
• 技术与定位争议：Firefox无法运行、Chrome兼容性问题；有人批评它并非真正的“字体”而是JS库，标题夸大，另有人原以为计算逻辑内置于字体中。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“概念创新”与“实际帮助/阅读干扰”的权衡，以及语义标注应由个人控制还是可能成为外部评价工具。

data.title: 9 Ads per Minute: FIFA Cup 26 – "the price of the beautiful game"
data.author: KellyCriterion
data.article_summary: 布里斯托大学与牛津大学研究发现，世界杯104场比赛直播中出现超过9.3万次有害商品品牌曝光，平均每7秒一次，其中不健康食品饮料占70.4%。相关广告覆盖近四分之一比赛时长，英国观众预计接触2670亿次。研究批评FIFA未利用广告替换技术，导致赌博、酒精等广告传播至受法律限制的国家，可能加剧儿童肥胖及社会、财务危害。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕世界杯比赛中广告/品牌标识的密集程度，以及AI视觉技术对广告曝光进行统计、审计和屏蔽的价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 技术应用派：AI分析了104场比赛、172.6小时画面，可量化广告曝光，帮助赞助商、审计机构核对合同，计算漏播损失；也可监测受限内容，减少人工审核。  
• 广告反感派：认为体育转播、球衣、球场、足球和球鞋到处都是营销信息，广告正在“淹没”观众；有人讽刺英超一边宣传社会正义，一边大量接受网络博彩赞助。  
• 影响有限派：部分人认为观众会自动忽略横幅和Logo，相比NFL频繁插播，球衣或场边广告并不算严重；也有人质疑统计数字是否遗漏了耐克、阿迪达斯等标识。  
• 研究质疑派：认为这项研究缺乏新意，甚至只是“边看世界杯边做研究”；核心问题应是禁止不合规商品，或接受广告存在。  
• 反广告技术派：提出在用户端实时识别并修补、替换植入广告，类似广告拦截；另有人推荐用AdGuard等工具屏蔽网络广告。  
• 反商业化派：认为营销只是价值抽取，对社会没有真正贡献，并批评FIFA及其资金、税务和商业运作。

补充讨论：评论还指出“补水暂停”可能源于商业转播对可预测广告时段的需求，显示赛事规则与广告利益存在联系。

49799083.article_content:
World Cup viewers exposed to junk food, alcohol and gambling branding every seven seconds, study finds
Press release issued:
22 September 2026
More than 93,000 visible appearances of brands promoting unhealthy food and drink, alcohol, gambling and speculative products were recorded during coverage of the largest FIFA World Cup in history, new research has found. Unhealthy food and drink brands accounted for more than seven in ten, with 65,722 appearances.
The research, led by the University of Bristol in collaboration with the
University of Oxford
, is the first to examine harmful commodity branding across an entire
FIFA
World Cup. The team used the UK’s most powerful supercomputer,
Isambard-AI
, based at University of Bristol, to analyse all 172.6 hours of live play across the tournament’s 104 matches.
The scale of potential exposure was extraordinary. FIFA reported that nearly six billion people around the world engaged with the tournament, while broadcast records were broken in more than 30 countries. For the UK, the researchers estimated that harmful product advertising generated 267 billion impressions across the 53 broadcasts for which audience data were available.
The analysis counted advertising built into the match footage (e.g. on the hoardings), rather than commercials shown during advertising breaks. Harmful product branding appeared in every match and was visible during 39.3 hours of live play, almost a quarter of all live play. Viewers could not avoid this marketing without also missing some of the football.
Unhealthy food and drink brands were found to dominate the tournament's sponsorship, representing more than seven in ten (70.4%) of all branding detected. This was followed by prediction markets with 9,360 appearances, alcohol with 9,266, gambling with 6,429 and cryptocurrency with 2,632.
Exposure was heavily concentrated among a handful of globally recognised brands. A familiar soft drink brand accounted for the highest number of logos (21,893), followed by a major fast-food chain (13,915), a sports drink brand (12,777), and a popular crisps brand (12,087). Together, these four brands were responsible for 65% of all harmful commodity logos recorded during the tournament.
Dr Raffaello Rossi
, Senior Lecturer in Marketing and Co-Director of the
Bristol Hub for Gambling Harms Research
at the University of Bristol, and co-author of the study, said: "As one of the world’s most watched sporting events, reaching billions of people, this year’s FIFA World Cup provided an unparalleled platform for advertising. Our findings reveal the sheer scale of branding embedded throughout tournament broadcasts, making exposure to unhealthy food, alcohol and gambling brands both omnipresent and unavoidable for viewers.
“This is particularly concerning given the substantial body of evidence linking marketing for unhealthy products, alcohol and gambling with increased consumption and a range of health, social and financial harms, especially among children and young people.”
Dr Elisa Becker
, Researcher,
Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences,
University of Oxford
, co-author of this study added: “We are facing a global crisis of childhood obesity and diet-related disease, yet the world’s biggest sporting event is saturated with marketing for unhealthy food and drinks. Sport should be part of the solution to poor health – not one of the world’s most powerful advertising platforms for the products driving it.”
A key issue highlighted by the research is that FIFA’s match footage, which featured the same embedded advertising around the pitch, was shared with broadcasters around the world, including in countries where alcohol, gambling or prediction markets advertising may be restricted or illegal.
Despite existing virtual board replacement technology which enables different advertising to be shown in different countries, findings from this report suggest FIFA’s commercial model failed to adequately account for national laws and cultural norms governing the promotion of harmful commodities. FIFA did not use this technology, and distributed World Cup footage containing embedded branding to countries where the use, advertisement, or purchase of some promoted products is not legal.
Dr Rossi added: “FIFA’s marketing deals appeared to show little respect for national laws and licensing regimes. The tournament featured around 16,000 gambling and prediction markets logos, with this advertising reaching a host of countries where the promoted brands were unlicensed, or where their legal status was uncertain. Indeed, one of the most advertised gambling brands listed licences in around 20 countries, while the World Cup was broadcast across more than 220 territories. Put plainly, audiences in the overwhelming majority of countries were shown advertising for a gambling operator that was not licensed locally.

data.title: What It's Like to Work in One of America's Data Centers
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据中心建设与运维工作的性质、职业体验、发展变化及其对选址和环境的影响。

不同观点：
• 一线工作者认为，数据中心相关岗位多为外包，涵盖布线、电工、安保等，收入差异大；工作环境炎热、脏累、压力大，电信行业尤其容易导致职业倦怠，但偶尔也有高薪和参与重要项目的成就感。  
• PaulRobinson回忆早期ISP：从农舍改机房、散热不足、木地板承重不够，到自建服务器、安装数万调制解调器，体现了早期数据中心简陋、快速扩张且高度依赖人工的特点；他认为那段经历虽艰苦，却有趣难忘，因此后来转向软件工作。  
• 有人质疑将一线人员统称为“工程师”，认为更准确的称呼可能是“技术员”。  
• 有评论认为现场工作内容单调，主要是巡查气味、噪声和设备异常，员工薪资约6.6万至12万美元；并批评相关故事带有数据中心政治议题炒作色彩。  
• 对选址存在分歧：有人质疑市中心建数据中心的必要性，认为城外的延迟劣势几乎可以忽略。  
• 另有评论关注数据中心的环境代价，询问其耗水、空气质量、湿度及用电是否造成重大影响。

补充讨论：评论横跨拨号网络时代与现代数据中心，反映技术进步、工作方式变化及“高技术设施”与实际苦工之间的反差。争议焦点主要是数据中心的真实职业价值、合理选址和环境影响。

data.title: MiMo-v2.6-Pro: Intelligence, Performance and Price Analysis
data.author: theanonymousone
data.article_summary: 文章评测了小米开源权重模型 MiMo-V2.6-Pro。该模型智能指数得分46，在同类模型中排名靠前；生成速度约111 tokens/秒，表现较快。输入价格为每百万tokens 0.435美元，输出价格0.87美元，成本适中但并非最低。模型支持文本、图像、语音和视频输入，具备100万tokens上下文窗口，总参数1万亿、激活参数420亿，采用MIT许可证。其主要缺点是输出较冗长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 MiMo-V2.6 Pro 的能力、速度、价格、评测排名及其与其他模型的比较展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极评价**：部分评论认为 MiMo-V2.6 Pro 是被低估的顶级模型，价格尤其有优势；其训练成本约347万美元，远低于大型模型常见的上亿美元成本，而缓存价格仅约0.0036美元/百万 tokens，性价比突出。  
• **谨慎评价性能**：有人认为它确实很强，但速度并不算快；自测中虽快于 DeepSeek，仍明显慢于领先模型。在 KillSwitch-Bench 中得分38.8，低于 Claude Opus 5、GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.1，但高于部分其他模型。  
• **使用体验问题**：MiMo 2.5 被认为适合一次性任务，但容易反复循环；用户希望 V2.6 已改善这一问题。也有人因 OpenAI 限额下降、表现不稳定，转而认真尝试中国模型，重点看重长期可预测性。  
• **质疑评测排名**：有人质疑 MiMo 在 Intelligence Index 得分46、高于 DeepSeek 的39是否合理，因为官方附录显示 DeepSeek 有时能超过 MiMo；此前 Opus 5 与 Fable 5 的排名也曾出现明显不符，说明榜单可能存在误差或方法问题。  
• **榜单与信息不完整**：评论质疑页面为何标为“AI领域第1/114”，但下方图表并不支持；另有人询问为何未纳入 Flash 模型及 Sol。

补充讨论：评测中 MiMo 生成约1.4亿 tokens，可能较为冗长；争议焦点主要是榜单可信度、模型真实能力与宣传排名是否一致。

49796660.article_summary: 文章评测了小米开源权重模型 MiMo-V2.6-Pro。该模型智能指数得分46，在同类模型中排名靠前；生成速度约111 tokens/秒，表现较快。输入价格为每百万tokens 0.435美元，输出价格0.87美元，成本适中但并非最低。模型支持文本、图像、语音和视频输入，具备100万tokens上下文窗口，总参数1万亿、激活参数420亿，采用MIT许可证。其主要缺点是输出较冗长。
49796660.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 MiMo-V2.6 Pro 的能力、速度、价格、评测排名及其与其他模型的比较展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极评价**：部分评论认为 MiMo-V2.6 Pro 是被低估的顶级模型，价格尤其有优势；其训练成本约347万美元，远低于大型模型常见的上亿美元成本，而缓存价格仅约0.0036美元/百万 tokens，性价比突出。  
• **谨慎评价性能**：有人认为它确实很强，但速度并不算快；自测中虽快于 DeepSeek，仍明显慢于领先模型。在 KillSwitch-Bench 中得分38.8，低于 Claude Opus 5、GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Fable 5.1，但高于部分其他模型。  
• **使用体验问题**：MiMo 2.5 被认为适合一次性任务，但容易反复循环；用户希望 V2.6 已改善这一问题。也有人因 OpenAI 限额下降、表现不稳定，转而认真尝试中国模型，重点看重长期可预测性。  
• **质疑评测排名**：有人质疑 MiMo 在 Intelligence Index 得分46、高于 DeepSeek 的39是否合理，因为官方附录显示 DeepSeek 有时能超过 MiMo；此前 Opus 5 与 Fable 5 的排名也曾出现明显不符，说明榜单可能存在误差或方法问题。  
• **榜单与信息不完整**：评论质疑页面为何标为“AI领域第1/114”，但下方图表并不支持；另有人询问为何未纳入 Flash 模型及 Sol。

补充讨论：评测中 MiMo 生成约1.4亿 tokens，可能较为冗长；争议焦点主要是榜单可信度、模型真实能力与宣传排名是否一致。

data.title: Can gzip be a language model?
data.author: networked
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个有趣实验：利用 gzip/DEFLATE 的压缩能力进行语言建模。压缩器会优先编码与语料库相似的字节序列，因此可用压缩后长度衡量候选文本的“可预测性”。作者结合滑动窗口和 beam search，让 gzip 根据莎士比亚语料续写文本。结果虽不连贯，却能体现语料特征，说明压缩与预测在实践中确实等价。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“压缩是否等同于语言建模”，讨论利用压缩率进行文本分类、生成与评估，以及传统压缩算法和大模型的关系。

不同观点：
• 支持压缩分类：可分别将测试文本与体育、政治、商业语料用 gzip 压缩，压缩后体积最小的类别即为判断结果；该思路与 Waikato 大学研究及 Hutter Prize 有关。  
• 语言即压缩：语言模型通过压缩文本捕捉规律，预测与压缩存在联系；但自然语言高度有损、持续演化，因此这种等价关系不稳定。数学证明因歧义更少，可能更适合体现压缩—预测关系。  
• 对“大模型≈压缩器”的谨慎态度：n-gram 或压缩模型与神经网络确有联系，但不能据此夸大二者性能接近；有人反问 LLM 相比 gzip 的实际压缩能力。  
• “提示词压缩代码/文本”的设想：若固定、可复现地用一个提示生成完整代码库，提示词是否算压缩仍有争议；依赖 git clone 则只是索引或下载，不是真正压缩。  
• 生成质量的质疑：gzip 搜索空间极大，beam search 是否接近全局最优并未说明，因此结果最多证明找到的序列可压缩，不能证明其最合理。文章还被批评未真正使用 gzip。  
• 跨模态与算法扩展：有人询问 JPEG、视频压缩能否成为视觉模型；也有人提及 zip2zip、bzip2、zstd 等工作。

补充讨论：不同算法优化的是不同统计结构：bzip2 生成重复字符，zstd 偏好空格和换行，未必像人类语言；争议焦点是“可压缩性”究竟代表语义、预测能力，还是仅代表编码器的偏好。

49797323.article_content:
A while back I wrote about
language modeling without neural networks
, where I generated Shakespeare with an unbounded n-gram model: no weights, no training, just counting. Fortuitously, I came across the paper
Language Modeling is Compression
, which mentioned the
compression–prediction equivalence
:
every prediction model is inherently a compressor, and all compression algorithms are prediction models
.
This led to the natural question:
can
gzip
do language modeling?
1
No neural network, no learned parameters, nothing. Just the compressor that ships with your operating system. You prime it with a corpus, give it a normal text prompt, and it continues that prompt by searching for the byte sequences that compress best. Here’s some real, unedited output after priming it on tiny Shakespeare:
gzipt --corpus data/tinyshakespeare.txt --prompt
$'MENENIUS:\n'
--length
200
MENENIUS:
'Though all at once canq
MARCIUS:
Pray now, nocamest thou to a morsel .
LARTIUS:
Hence, and
I' the end admire, where G
again; and after it ag .
It turns out, kind of? It’s not exactly coherent text, but it clearly
knows
something about the text. Much more than I expected
gzip
to
know
.
2
So how can a compressor generate this?
Compression is prediction
#
Think about what a compressor does. It spends few bytes on data it “expects” and many bytes on data it doesn’t. If I hand you a file that’s the letter
A
repeated a million times, you can describe it in one sentence. A million random bytes, on the other hand, have no structure to exploit and barely compress at all.
This is not a coincidence; it’s the core of information theory. The number of bits needed to encode a symbol is $-\log_2 p$, where $p$ is the probability the model assigns to it. High probability means few bits. So any compressor has a probability model hiding inside it, whether or not anyone wrote one down.
gzip
uses
DEFLATE
, which compresses the next bytes by finding matches against the recent text in a 32 KiB sliding window. If a continuation echoes something already in the window, DEFLATE encodes it as a cheap back-reference instead of literal bytes. So:
A continuation that gzip “expected”, because it echoes text already in its window, compresses to almost nothing.
That gives us a score. If I have some context and I want to know how good a candidate continuation is, I just measure:
$$\text{score}(\text{candidate}) = \texttt{len(gzip(context + candidate))}$$
The smaller the compressed length, the more “predicted” the candidate is. To prime the model, I include a corpus in gzip’s window. Any continuation that looks like the corpus compresses small, and any continuation that doesn’t compresses large.
Generating by beam search
#
Scoring is one thing; generating is another. The naive approach of picking the single next byte that compresses best fails badly, and for a subtle reason: gzip only gives an integer byte length (no fractions). Adding one byte often doesn’t change the compressed length at all, so many candidates tie and the signal is buried in quantization noise.
The fix is to look
ahead
a whole span before committing.
gzipt
runs a
beam search
over byte sequences. At each step, the current context is:
corpus window + recent tail of (prompt + generated bytes)
Then
gzipt
tries possible next bytes. Each candidate continuation is scored by compressing
context + candidate
and checking how many bytes the compressed result takes.
The loop is:
Prompt.
Start with the user’s prompt as the initial text to continue. There is no start token; the prompt bytes are just part of the context gzip sees.
Context.
Show gzip the corpus window plus the recent tail of the prompt/generated text.
Search.
Keep the
beam_width
most-compressible partial continuations. Extend each by every byte that occurs in the corpus, score all of them by compressed length, and prune back down to the best
beam_width
. Repeat for
horizon
bytes.
Commit.
Take the most-compressible full span (or sample among the finalists if
temperature
is positive), append it, and start the loop over.
One detail that matters is that
only the last
tail
bytes of generated output stay in the scoring context.
DEFLATE codes nearby matches more cheaply than far ones, so if gzip could see its entire history, the cheapest thing to do is often to fall into verbatim loops, repeatedly copying text it just emitted.
You can see the decoding and scoring process in the animation above, which is the same replay shown at the top. The whole thing is one file of pure standard-library Python (just
zlib
). Code’s on
GitHub
if you want to play with it.
The paper did try this, but it ended up performing poorly. Adding beam search significantly improved generation quality (an idea they mentioned), which is discussed below.
↩︎
The code actually uses zlib instead of spawning a gzip process, but the name GziPT was too good. I believe they both use the same DEFLATE algorithm under the hood.
↩︎

data.title: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You
data.author: dimonomid
data.article_summary: 文章认为，AI虽能提升编码效率，但放弃读写代码和代码评审将导致项目逐渐失控。代码可维护性难以即时衡量，AI缺乏判断优良架构的能力，生成代码常难理解、难演进。过度依赖AI还会阻碍开发者积累经验、承担责任并走向精通。作者主张将AI作为工具而非替代者，并预测“无AI”政策未来可能成为企业竞争优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI 编程的效率提升与代码质量、工程责任及行业知识传承之间的冲突。

不同观点：
• **谨慎派**：过度依赖 AI 会削弱开发者和组织的制度性知识，类似制造业外包后失去生产能力；若无人理解系统，银行结算、医疗设备、敏感数据删除等高风险场景难以追责。  
• **工具派**：AI 不必然导致不可维护代码。通过规范、测试、架构约束及 SonarQube 等指标，可将 AI 纳入良好工程流程；而人类长期以来也一直制造糟糕的遗留系统。  
• **实践支持派**：有经验者可借助 AI 快速完成复杂项目，把精力转向产品路线、正确性和验证。数据库项目案例显示，作者几乎不读生成代码，却通过测试和迭代获得了更强产出。  
• **乐观自动化派**：资本和技术势头不会放缓，未来多数开发者可能不再手写代码，甚至架构设计也会被自动化；坚持人工编码者将像手工鞋匠一样成为小众。  
• **反思与怀疑派**：简单提示只能产出“能运行但没有未来”的原型，LLM 缺乏真正意图，最终责任仍需由人承担。有人预测“No-AI”会成为卖点，但也有人认为难以验证其真实性，且模型进步会使该趋势落空。

补充讨论：争议核心是“效率是否值得牺牲知识、可维护性与责任”。讨论还涉及 AI 学到的是网络上普遍但未必优质的代码，以及软件可复制性远高于实体工厂所引发的职业与价值焦虑。

49799965.article_content:
In the past month alone I’ve heard these phrases:
I haven’t written code since 2025
;
Code reviews are dead
;
People no longer read code
.
Certainly the industry is transforming, however, the people and organizations falling into the trap of no longer reading and writing code only do so at their peril.
Fact is, vibe-coded projects devolve over time into an unmaintainable mess. The reason is simple, yet hard to fix: code maintainability and good architecture don’t have good measurements that we can apply, because it takes months, years even, to notice the effects of bad architecture or of unmaintainable code.
We can certainly define bad code: code that’s hard to read, hard to understand, hard to evolve for whatever the future throws our way. The kind of code in which changing one thing breaks the program in very non-deterministic ways, or breaks the logic somewhere else, far removed from your change, resembling the “butterfly effect”. The kind of code where adding a feature means a serious undertaking due to changing code in multiple places and still forgetting to patch everything, thus getting inconsistencies. Code in which the invariants of the design aren’t clear, with its authors no longer being around to guard against violations and ensure some coherence. Code that is hard to test, requiring mocks and exposing implementation details, leading to fragile tests that end up preventing meaningful refactoring.
And yet, we know it as a fact that noticing bad code takes time. Months, years. Of course, the experienced software engineers have a nose that can detect code smells and can take action long before the bad effects can be observed.
The proficient developers, the experts, rely on their intuition built with sweat and tears, working long hours trying to debug and fix production issues, swearing to never again be so foolish as to repeat past mistakes. It’s the kind of intuition that can’t really be made into a list of rigid rules, because everything is context-dependent. Experts are incompatible with the same rules and recipes that make beginners more productive.
Experts don’t follow the rules, they make the rules.
And so we have a problem…
For one, AI is not trained on what it means for code to be maintainable. For instance, any reinforcement learning done needs a reward signal that can be measured immediately, not in months or years. The AI learns rules from rulebooks meant for beginners. The AI notices patterns from code in the wild and let’s be honest, most code in the wild is pretty bad. There is no fitness function you can define for maintainable code, at least not one that we can discern, otherwise it would’ve been baked into our linters.
Have you noticed how terrible is the AI at “simplifying” code? Yes, the SOTA models. It can’t even define functions properly, choosing to split functions into smaller functions that are not actually reusable. Extracting a smaller function from a bigger function is a very bad choice if, to understand the bigger function, you have to also read the implementation of the extracted smaller function. Defining reusable and clarifying functions is an art form, an art that takes mastery. Most developers, being still
“advanced beginners”
in the
Dreyfus model
, are not able to define good, clarifying, reusable functions and neither does the AI currently.
This wouldn’t be so bad if people would still be in control and learn from those mistakes. But we are seeing a trend of people relying on AI to write, and even read code.
Those people will never reach mastery, because they no longer make choices, they no longer take responsibility for mistakes in coding and no longer learn from those mistakes. It’s the AI that’s making mistakes now, the AI doesn’t learn from those mistakes, and neither are the people relying on AI for coding.
Yikes!
Don’t get me wrong, I think LLMs are a great tool. I’m no Luddite, I’ve integrated AI in my everyday work, while actually teaching my colleagues what I’ve learned. I gladly use LLMs to take care of all the boring, soul-sucking shit we have to deal with. I’m also enjoying the efficiency benefits that I’m seeing. But at the end of the day, it’s just a tool, and like all other revolutions, its light will also fade; IMO, it already is, as right now tech news is frankly quite boring.
People are actually terrible at making predictions. I believe the future will surprise all of us. But, I’m going to make a prediction of my own…
In the future we will see more and more companies proudly boasting their “NO-AI” policy as a competitive advantage. And they will be right.
“But automated assembly lines are always more efficient”
people say, except that the software industry is special, because we’ve always done automation at scale, everything we do is automation, LLMs are not the only means for it, and depending on context, it may actually be a distraction.
“Coding isn’t solved”
in any meaningful sense. Sure, you can instruct the LLM to build you a C/C++ compiler,

data.title: I said no and Apple said yes
data.author: thatslast
data.article_summary: 文章批评苹果在 macOS 27 升级后重新启用 Apple Intelligence，移除或隐藏关闭选项，并留下无法终止的 Siri 进程及占用 22.28GB 的数据。作者认为这侵犯用户隐私与选择权，反映整个 AI 行业无视“同意”，强迫用户接受服务，并伴随内容安全、消费者伤害和数据盗用等问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Apple Intelligence/macOS 的默认启用、数据透明度、用户同意权及“大公司强推 AI”展开争论。

不同观点：
• **批评用户控制权不足**：多位评论者认为 Apple 不提供真正的“拒绝”选项，常以“稍后再说”代替彻底关闭；即使关闭 Siri 和相关开关，部分 AI、照片功能及后台进程仍会存在，体现出对用户意愿的不尊重。  
• **担忧隐私与系统敌意化**：评论将 Apple、Windows 等系统视为广告、遥测和数据收集驱动的“用户不友好环境”，认为个人电脑正从“个人设备”变成由平台控制的产品。  
• **对文章事实的纠正**：Coeur 指出，Apple Intelligence Report 的 15 分钟/7 天选项是供用户查看已发送数据的透明度报告，并非按该频率额外向 Apple 发送个人数据，因此文章关于“每 15 分钟回传数据”的核心结论可能不准确。  
• **主张抵制或转向替代品**：有人推荐 Linux、GrapheneOS，甚至减少社交媒体、流媒体和 SaaS 使用；也有人认为 Linux 虽较开放，但同样受到企业利益影响。  
• **提供技术绕过方案**：包括用 Apple Configurator 配置文件禁用 AI、修改地区以限制 Siri、通过 Firefox 设置关闭同步菜单，以及寻找不下载 AI 模型的办法。  
• **主张监管介入**：建议法律要求系统安装和更新时必须提供明确的拒绝选项，类似欧盟浏览器选择规则。

back in June it became obvious Apple does not âthink different.â

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：记忆宫殿及联想、编码等技巧能否有效记忆数字，以及其实际价值和适用人群。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为感官、具体、荒诞甚至“色情”的形象比抽象数字更易记忆；可用记忆宫殿、数字—字母映射和故事串联数字。有人借此记住购物清单、门锁密码，或在法学考试中记住约250个案例。  
• 有人认为无需复杂技巧，重复练习、歌曲或押韵文本同样有效；评论中有人靠重复记住50—120位圆周率，也有儿童通过歌曲记住100位甚至更多。  
• 反对或质疑者认为记住100位圆周率不算“超能力”，现实用途有限，记忆技巧未必能提升一般认知能力；有人认为学习乐曲可能更值得。  
• Aphantasia（无法形成视觉意象）者指出，记忆宫殿要求同时记住地点和物品，反而增加负担，因此方法并不普适。

Engineering Memory
Thoughts on learning to memorize the first one hundred digits of pi.
Published
21 December 2024
About three years ago, I memorized the first one hundred digits of pi. I did it on a lark, after reading Joshua Foerâs
Moonwalking with Einstein
. The bookâs
central claim is that nearly anyone can achieve seemingly super-human feats of
memory with proper technique and deliberate
practice. Intrigued, I put the some of the
techniques to the test and found that they worked surprisingly well. But they
did not just work. They converted the hard and shapeless problem of how to
remember into a problem of discipline and methodology. Remembering became engineering.
The central insight behind most memory techniques is an observation: the human
brain is not bad at memorization per se; it is only bad at memorizing specific
kinds of information. For
example, you can probably only hold
5-9
objects
in short-term memory, but you can visualize your childhood home with relative clarity. And most adults have well-developed memories for certain
topics, such as a car mechanic for car engines. In absolute bits of information, we can hold a lot in our minds, but we
struggle when that information lacks meaning or context.
Memorization techniques harness this observation with a method called
elaborative
encoding
. The basic idea is to associate hard-to-remember objects with easy-to-remember
objects. Perhaps the most famous example of this technique is called the
method of
loci
. In this
technique, you place objects you want to remember in a visually familiar place
called a
memory palace
. And then recall is just the act of âwalkingâ
through a memory palace in your mind and visualizing each object.
To memorize digits of pi, I used a more modern and advanced technique designed
specifically for memorizing numbers, called a
person-action-object
(PAO) system. In a
PAO, one associates each digit in the set

action to an object. Then any six-digit number one wishes to memorize is encoded as the person from
the first two digits doing the action from the second two digits to the object
in the third two digits. Iâll call this combined image representing six digits a âglpyhâ. For example,
in my memory palace for pi, I have the glpyh:
Albert Einstein
twirling a leotard

are powerful because they automate the process of coming up with elaborative
encodings. And since you have one hundred persons, actions, and objects, you
have one million unique and ideally memorable glyphs.

seventeen glpyhs. These fit into a
relatively small memory palaceâin my case, in the apartment of an old friend.
Obviously, the harder task was memorizing my PAO, since that requires memorizing
one hundred âbaseâ glpyhs! In fact, probably the
single most time-consuming task of memorizing pi was not even memorizing my PAO
but simply building my PAO in a spreadsheet. This is because each person,

data.article_summary: 文章称，OpenAI雇用数千名承包商审核用户对话、评价模型回答，却有多名承包商因在工作中使用AI而被解雇。公司明确禁止使用生成式AI，并通过审查文字风格、标点和完成速度等方式识别违规。此事凸显“用AI训练AI”的讽刺，也引发对模型崩溃、数据真实性及承包商工作处境的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI承包商使用AI完成原本要求人工完成的数据标注，引发对人工反馈必要性、规则执行及“用AI训练AI”逻辑的讨论。

不同观点：
• **规则与质量立场**：承包商受雇提供不借助AI的真实人类反馈，却违规使用AI，因此被终止合同；人工反馈对训练仍很重要，AI循环生成可能导致低质量、不可读内容。  
• **质疑新闻价值**：有人认为这是明确的合同违约，事件本身并不新鲜，标题却带有“点击诱饵”色彩。  
• **技术路线质疑**：事件被解读为OpenAI并不相信单靠模型递归自我改进，仍需“蒸馏人类大脑”而非仅使用自身权重。  
• **讽刺与行业批评**：批评AI公司一边鼓吹用AI替代人类，一边因人类用AI辅助工作而解雇他们，被视为AI泡沫破裂或行业自相矛盾的表现。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于，使用AI是否违背了数据标注任务的核心目的，以及公司强调人工价值时是否存在双重标准。

People Training OpenAI’s AI Fired for Using AI to Train the AI
Joseph Cox

OpenAI has thousands and thousands of contractors helping improve the company's AI models. Multiple contractors have been fired for using AI to train the AI.
IMAGE: SPUMONI COOPERATIVE FOR 404 MEDIA.
OpenAI has an army of contractors who read real ChatGPT users’ prompts and other data to help improve the chatbot’s responses. The idea is that the contractors provide an, obviously, human touch to OpenAI’s models. Well, not all of the contractors are doing that. 404 Media has found multiple contractors hired to improve OpenAI’s models have been fired for using AI to train the AI. That’s not great for the models themselves, but there is also obviously a great irony in AI training companies working for OpenAI firing people for using AI when OpenAI’s whole thing is to make people use AI at work.
Some AI models already exhibit signs of
“model collapse,”
which is where AI models further trained on AI-generated text can become worse and worse. In this case, some of the people hired to partially stop that happening are themselves using AI-generated responses to train OpenAI’s models.
One contractor said they see people using AI “all the time and people are let go for it all the time, it’s pretty much the one thing that will get you kicked off ASAP.” The person said, “in a group of thousands there are tons that have been caught.”
💡
Do you work as a prompt reviewer for OpenAI, Anthropic, or another AI company? I would love to hear from you. Using a non-work device, you can message me securely on Signal at joseph.404 or send me an email at joseph@404media.co.
Last week,
404 Media revealed
Project Lily, in which OpenAI has hundreds of contractors reading real ChatGPT users’ prompts and conversations which can include personal information. Those contractors then rate and critique the responses ChatGPT generated, including making sure that the responses are not too sycophantic or anthropomorphize ChatGPT. That reporting was based on internal documents and conversations with a person who works on the prompts.
404 Media has now obtained other internal documents and spoken to three contractors doing work for OpenAI across various projects. Those projects can include more than ten thousand contractors, according to one of the internal documents.
One of those documents says contractors must not use AI themselves for their work.
“Do not use AI detection tools, or AI yourself,” one document describing the work of contractors who are hired to review the work of other contractors, including catching them for using AI, says. “Do not use GPTZero or any other AI detection tool. They are not reliable. Reviewers may not use AI either, including Grammarly and AI translation, to review, write feedback, or write comments.”
The document continues, “Do not tell evaluators why you suspect AI. It is easier for them to hide if they know what you look for. Judge the overall pattern, not one clue.”
All three of the contractors said reviewers are told not to use AI in their work. Two of the sources said people have been fired or offboarded for using AI. 404 Media granted the contractors anonymity as they weren’t permitted to speak to the press.
The contractors who review other contractors’ work are told to be on the look out for tell-tale signs of AI use. That can include repetitive words, AI-style punctuation — which might include over zealous use of the em dash — and contractors finishing their work very quickly.
In related Slack channels where people ask each other for advice, a lot of people will post an example with the question, ‘Is this AI?,’ one contractor said.
“Usually the answer is yes,” the person said.
One contractor said they used AI while helping to train OpenAI’s models and shared what they presented as their termination letter. It said their employer had identified issues with the “authenticity” of their work.
“I’m not a bad person or worker. I just needed a little boost and turned to AI to help me which eventually led to my downfall,” the contractor told 404 Media. “I felt no joy in the work or that I was contributing to society in any way.”
Two of the contractors 404 Media spoke to worked for Mercor, an AI-training company that hires the contractors who in turn review ChatGPT-related material. A Mercor spokesperson told 404 Media in a statement: “Our experts are hired for their expertise and judgement, which is essential to the ongoing advancement of AI. Our contracts strictly prohibit the use of LLMs to complete projects and we enforce that. We invest heavily in our tools and systems to detect misuse and ensure our experts comply with project rules and contract terms. When we confirm an expert has used AI to complete a task, we immediately remove them from the project.”
